subject: Quarter stage-gate: sales runway deepnotes & owner checklist
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 7 Sep 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quarter stage-gate: sales runway deepnotes & owner checklist

Team —

As we lock the QBR deck this week I want to collect a tight, account-by-account digest for the runway section. Please do the following by EOD Monday (Sep 11):

- Fill the attached qbr_account_digest_template.docx for each named account you own. Keep it to one page: ARR change (net-new/expansion/churn), primary risk, next milestone, and ask.
- Update the 2028_Q3_runway_consolidation_v1.xlsx with your forecast adjustments (probability and expected close date). I care about per-account assumptions not just rollups.
- Flag any deals where we need SLA or pricing exceptions (I will push to Finance/Legal).

For the leadership slide I want: top 8 runway accounts called out with one-paragraph risk blurbs, plus a short executive summary that explains delta vs last quarter's forecast and drivers.

Attachments: qbr_account_digest_template.docx (template), runway spreadsheet (placeholder).

Why: execs want confidence on each named deal and a clear set of mitigations; we cannot surface a single aggregated number without line-of-sight on assumptions.

Questions? If you have missing data for an account, mark it and add the missing field (owner + ask) so I can follow up.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 7 Sep 2028 09:27:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarter stage-gate: sales runway deepnotes & owner checklist

Karthik —

Got it. I started a tabbed sheet with owner routing and raw ARR pulls. Quick notes on owners I already spoke with:

- Acme Analytics (Beth Turner): expansion + dedicated capacity ask; likely Q4 close but under risk for delivery timing.
- Veridian Health: reshaped opportunity; moving from pilot to PoC — probability reduced to 35%.
- Nimbus Retail: deal team requesting extended trial; likely push to Oct.

I'll attach the first pass of the consolidated workbook and a short owner map. I'll also prod owners to return the one-pagers and will flag anything missing by EOD Monday.

Attachment: 2028_Q3_runway_consolidation_v1.xlsx (v0.9)

-Marissa
Sr. Manager, Sales Strategy

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Sep 2028 10:05:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarter stage-gate: sales runway deepnotes & owner checklist

Thanks Marissa —

Two asks from the field that should change how we present the runway:

1) Probability buckets: please include an adjacent column for lead reason (e.g., "waiting KCS/SOC2 evidence", "procurement timing", "exec sponsor alignment") so the exec readout can understand controllable vs timing risks.
2) For Acme specifically: they want a committed delivery window for Dedicated (they're pricing our SLA ask against a known timeline). Can we surface an ETA or a caveat that timelines are contingent on infra readiness?

I will fill in Nimbus and Veridian one-pagers tonight.

-Tessa
VP, Enterprise Sales

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Sep 2028 13:15:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarter stage-gate: sales runway deepnotes & owner checklist

Attaching the consolidated workbook with owner notes filled for all accounts I touched. Key changes in v1.1:

- Added "lead reason" column per Tessa's ask; populated for Acme, Veridian, Nimbus, and three other mid-market accounts.
- Normalized estimated close week to ISO week numbers to make the slide-friendly aggregation easier.
- Marked Acme as "delivery-dependent" and attached acme_execution_timeline.pdf with the customer-provided target dates.

Attachment: 2028_Q3_runway_consolidation_v1.xlsx (v1.1)

Questions: Please review the Acme notes — we should decide whether to include them in "top 8" or call them out separately as a dependent expansion.

-Aditya
Sales Engineer Lead

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Sep 2028 16:02:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarter stage-gate: sales runway deepnotes & owner checklist

Team —

Thanks for the fast turn. Readouts for execs should follow this structure:

- Slide 1: Top-line delta vs. last quarter (delta by motion: net-new vs expansion vs churn). One bullet explanation per driver.
- Slide 2: Top 8 runway accounts (one-line risk + ask). If Acme stays delivery-dependent we will call it out in a separate "execution contingent" box and exclude from the 8.
- Slide 3: Consolidated close distribution (by week) and the list of deals >$250k with current probability.

I'll pull the v1.1 workbook and create the executive summary. Next steps: Marissa finalize owners and one-pagers; Tessa and Aditya please confirm Acme handling and whether to include the ACME slide with a mitigation plan.

I'll prepare a 3-bullet exec summary and a recommended ask (credits / SLA exception) to present to the Revenue Committee.

Karthik

From: Beth Turner <beth@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: acctops@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Sat, 8 Sep 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarter stage-gate: sales runway deepnotes & owner checklist

Karthik —

Thanks for the outreach and for noting Acme as delivery-dependent. A few clarifications from our side:

- We need a committed 8-week window for Dedicated capacity post-SOW signature to align with our go-live calendar. Can Redwood confirm whether that ETA is realistic given your Q4 backlog?
- We are evaluating two pricing scenarios; the preferred one ties pricing to delivery commitments. If an SLA exception is required we'll escalate internally.

I'll work with our procurement team (cc'd) to surface the timeline constraints. Please let me know if Redwood has a standard SLA exception playbook to accelerate internal approvals.

Best,
Beth Turner
Dir. of Cloud Ops, Acme Analytics
